name: indiquant-mcp

tools.name: get_current_round
tools.description: Read the latest round on a track ('core' or 'sprint'): its id, state, whether the submission window is open, and the submission deadline in both IST and UTC. Read-only; spends nothing. 'Current' means the most recently opened round, which may already be LOCKED — check window_open.

tools.name: get_round_status
tools.description: Read one round's state and schedule by round_id (window open or closed, deadline in IST and UTC, resolve date, universe size). Read-only.

tools.name: get_round_descriptor
tools.description: Read a round's dataset descriptor: universe size, feature list, the file's sha256 fingerprint and the dataset version label (the version whose training data matches the round). Universe ids are included only when include_universe=true. Read-only; opens no data session and returns no feature values.

tools.name: get_scoring_rules
tools.description: Read the platform's published scoring rules document (what is measured, what is ranked, the turnover charge). Read-only.

tools.name: get_data_access_terms
tools.description: Read the versioned data-access terms every download is subject to (SDK-only access, install keys, session limits, attribution marks, permitted use), and whether the user's account has accepted the version in force. Read-only. Show these to the user before a first download. No tool can accept them: if they are not accepted, the user runs `indiquant-mcp accept-terms` in their own terminal.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the signed-in contributor's models (model_id, public display name, active). There is no limit on how many models an account holds. Read-only.

tools.name: create_model
tools.description: Create a new model under the signed-in account. SIDE EFFECT: creates a model for good (it can be retired, not deleted), and display_name becomes a public, platform-unique leaderboard handle. There is no cap on models; at most 20 may be created a day. Without confirm=true it only previews and returns a confirmation_token. Show the user the name, and call again with confirm=true and that confirmation_token only after the user explicitly agrees; a missing or stale token is refused.

tools.name: list_install_keys
tools.description: List the install keys registered to this account (key_id, label, fingerprint, live or revoked, last used), marking the one this machine holds. Read-only.

tools.name: revoke_install_key
tools.description: Revoke one install key by key_id. SIDE EFFECT: irreversible; closes every data session that key opened, and if it is this machine's key, downloads stop until the user runs `indiquant-mcp login` in a terminal. Without confirm=true it only previews and returns a confirmation_token; ask the user, then call again with confirm=true, the same reason, and that confirmation_token.

tools.name: download_round_features
tools.description: Download a round's feature file to a local path the user names (out_path ending .parquet or .csv). SIDE EFFECTS: opens one signed data session (the account may open 48 per rolling 24 hours) unless this round was already downloaded, in which case the cached copy is reused and nothing is opened; writes a file. Returns only a summary (rows, column count, feature list, universe size, dataset version, path) — never feature values. Rows stay in the session's own order; do not ask for them to be sorted or printed.

tools.name: download_training_data
tools.description: Download a dataset version's training artefact to a local path the user names (.parquet or .csv). SIDE EFFECTS: opens one signed data session unless this version is already cached; writes a file. Returns only a summary (rows, column count, feature list, eras) — never data values. Get the version label from get_round_descriptor's dataset_version.

tools.name: validate_predictions
tools.description: Check a local predictions file (CSV or parquet with exactly the columns id,score) against a round's universe using the same validator the platform runs. Returns the full report: coverage, duplicates, unknown ids, non-finite or constant scores, payload size. Sends nothing.

tools.name: export_predictions_csv
tools.description: Normalise a local id,score file (CSV or parquet) into the exact CSV the website's upload form accepts: header 'id,score', one row per universe id in universe order. Validates first and writes nothing if validation fails. SIDE EFFECT: writes out_path. Sends nothing.

tools.name: submit_predictions
tools.description: Submit a local predictions file (exact id,score header) for a round and model. It is validated locally first and never sent if validation fails. SIDE EFFECT when confirm=true: replaces any earlier submission of this model for this round (there is no per-round attempt limit; at most 30 uploads an hour per model). Always call first WITHOUT confirm: the preview returns a confirmation_token bound to the round, the model and the file's scores. Show the user the round, the model and the row count it returns, ask whether to proceed, and only after the user explicitly says yes call again with confirm=true and that confirmation_token. If the file changed since the preview, or no preview was made, the call is refused and nothing is sent. Returns the receipt, a check that its sha256 matches the local float32 digest, and the platform's immediate feedback (insight: feature exposure, near-duplicates of your other models, notes).

tools.name: get_scores
tools.description: Read a model's resolved round scores (most recent first, up to limit). Read-only.

tools.name: get_trust
tools.description: Read a model's latest trust snapshot (posterior mean, sd, rounds counted, status). Read-only.

tools.name: get_model_report
tools.description: Read one model's performance report (model_id or display name): the headline (sector-neutral CORR latest, 10-round mean, hit rate, trend), per-round scores with their diagnostics, how it did by market regime and dispersion, cost realism, its standing, when pending rounds will be scored, and rule-based 'what to try next' advice with the evidence behind each item. Fields still under the platform's display delay are null. Read-only.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Read all of the signed-in contributor's models side by side: each model's headline, latest scored round, pending rounds and the next score date, and which of them are near-duplicates of each other. Also states the grant rule (one grant per contributor per cycle, from the best model). Read-only.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Read the most recently published leaderboard for a track ('core' or 'sprint'), up to limit rows. Read-only.

tools.name: run_local_model
tools.description: Run the user's own local Python script (script_path ending .py) as a subprocess, with a timeout, to produce predictions: it is invoked with the Python interpreter this server runs on, as `python SCRIPT --features FEATURES_PATH --out OUT_PATH --round-id ROUND_ID` (the same values are also in the environment as INDIQUANT_FEATURES_PATH, INDIQUANT_PREDICTIONS_PATH, INDIQUANT_ROUND_ID; no other INDIQUANT_ variable is passed) and must write an id,score CSV to OUT_PATH, which must end .csv. An existing OUT_PATH is replaced only with overwrite=true. SIDE EFFECTS: executes local code; writes OUT_PATH and a .log beside it. Returns only the exit status and the validation summary — never the script's output or the data. Sends nothing.

instructions: Tools for the IndiQuant research tournament, running locally over the contributor's own SDK session. Rules: (1) never ask the user for a password or token — if a tool says the user is not signed in, tell them to run `indiquant-mcp login` in a terminal; (2) dataset files are written to paths the user chooses and only summaries come back — do not try to read feature values into the conversation, and do not re-sort a downloaded file; (3) predictions come from a file on disk with the exact header id,score — never write prediction values yourself; (4) validate before submitting, and never call submit_predictions with confirm=true until the user has seen the round, model and row count and said yes; pass back the confirmation_token the preview returned (create_model and revoke_install_key work the same way). A new upload replaces the model's earlier one for the round; there is no per-round attempt limit (at most 30 uploads an hour per model). Scores are ranks: only the ordering matters. For how a model is doing and what to try next, use get_model_report and get_overview.
